title: Lifespan single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human prefrontal cortex
title_zh: 人类前额叶皮层单细胞全寿命转录组图谱
abstract: The human brain undergoes profound changes from early development through late adulthood, shaping cognition, behaviour and vulnerability to disease1,2. Understanding how these changes are organized within specific brain regions and cell types is essential for interpreting normal ageing and its relationship to psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex has a central role in higher cognitive functions and is particularly sensitive to age-related decline3, yet its cellular and molecular programs across the human lifespan remain poorly defined. Most existing studies4–7 have focused on restricted age ranges or disease-affected brains, limiting the ability to distinguish normative developmental and ageing trajectories from pathological processes. Consequently, a comprehensive, lifespan-resolved reference of cellular states in the human prefrontal cortex has been lacking. Here, using a single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas spanning the human lifespan, we show that the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex exhibits non-linear, cell-type-specific transcriptional trajectories characterized by dynamic remodelling during development, relative stability in midlife and selective molecular reactivation in late adulthood. We identify distinct neuronal and glial programs, including early-life neuronal resilience pathways and late-life glial programs associated with immune activation, stress responses and circadian reorganization. These programs are anatomically organized across cortical layers and grey–white matter domains, revealing coordinated spatial and molecular changes. Together, these findings provide a framework for understanding how cellular programs transition from resilience to vulnerability in the human cortex and establish a foundation for interpreting age-related cognitive decline and disease risk. The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex exhibits non-linear, cell-type-specific transcriptional trajectories characterized by dynamic remodelling during development, relative stability in midlife and selective molecular reactivation in late adulthood.
abstract_zh: 人类大脑从早期发育到晚年经历深刻变化，塑造认知、行为和疾病易感性1,2。理解这些变化在特定脑区和细胞类型内的组织方式，对于解释正常衰老及其与精神和神经退行性疾病的关系至关重要。背外侧前额叶皮层在高级认知功能中起中心作用，且对年龄相关衰退特别敏感3，然而其在人类全寿命中的细胞和分子程序仍知之甚少。现有大多数研究4–7已局限于特定年龄范围或疾病大脑，限制了区分正常发育和衰老轨迹与病理过程的能力。因此，迟迟未能获得一份涵盖人类前额叶皮层全寿命的细胞状态综合参考资料。在此，我们利用跨越人类全寿命的单核转录组图谱，展示背外侧前额叶皮层表现出非线性、细胞类型特异性的转录轨迹，其特征是发育过程中的动态重塑、中年相对稳定以及晚年选择性的分子重激活。我们鉴定出不同的神经元和胶质程序，包括早期神经元韧性通路和晚期与免疫激活、应激反应及昼夜节律重组相关的胶质程序。这些程序在皮层层和灰白质域中呈空间组织分布，揭示了协调的空间和分子变化。这些发现共同提供了一个框架，用于理解人类皮层中细胞程序从韧性向脆弱的转变，并为解释年龄相关认知衰退和疾病风险奠定了基础。背外侧前额叶皮层表现出非线性、细胞类型特异性的转录轨迹，其特征是发育过程中的动态重塑、中年相对稳定以及晚年选择性的分子重激活。
